We need to simplify the product:
$$P = (2+1)(2^2+1)(2^4+1)(2^8+1)\cdots(2^{256}+1)$$

The exponents are 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256. So the product is:
$$P = \prod_{k=0}^{8} (2^{2^k} + 1)$$

This is a classic problem where we use the identity:
$$(x-1)(x+1)(x^2+1)(x^4+1)\cdots(x^{2^n}+1) = x^{2^{n+1}} - 1$$
Here $x = 2$ and $n = 8$ (since the exponents go from $2^0 = 1$ to $2^8 = 256$).
answer_text:
# Simplifying the Product

## Identifying the Pattern

The product is:
$$P = (2+1)(2^2+1)(2^4+1)(2^8+1)\cdots(2^{256}+1) = \prod_{k=0}^{8}\left(2^{2^k}+1\right)$$

## Using the Difference of Squares Chain

I recall the key identity: multiplying each factor by $(x-1)$ triggers a telescoping chain via the difference of squares:

$$\begin{aligned}
(x-1)(x+1) &= x^2 - 1 \\
(x^2-1)(x^2+1) &= x^4 - 1 \\
(x^4-1)(x^4+1) &= x^8 - 1 \\
&\;\;\vdots \\
(x^{2^n}-1)(x^{2^n}+1) &= x^{2^{n+1}} - 1
\end{aligned}$$

So in general:
$$(x-1)\prod_{k=0}^{n}(x^{2^k}+1) = x^{2^{n+1}}-1$$

## Applying to Our Problem

Set $x = 2$ and $n = 8$ (the exponents run from $2^0 = 1$ to $2^8 = 256$):

$$(2-1)\cdot P = 2^{2^9} - 1 = 2^{512} - 1$$

Since $2 - 1 = 1$:

$$P = 2^{512} - 1$$

## Verification (Small Case)

For the first three factors: $(2+1)(2^2+1)(2^4+1) = 3 \times 5 \times 17 = 255 = 2^8 - 1$. ✓

This matches the formula with $n=2$: $2^{2^3}-1 = 2^8-1 = 255$. ✓

## Result

$$\boxed{2^{512}-1}$$
